issue.title: test_facade_try_disable_one_winner_under_process_contention flakes under the full parallel lane: a 2s start-file poll and 10s communicate timeout across 6 spawned interpreters
issue.description:
`tests/test_provider_disable.py::test_facade_try_disable_one_winner_under_process_contention`
failed once in a full parallel `just test` run on a clean master tree
(HEAD ad9ed74af, no local diff) and passed 5/5 on immediate serial reruns of
the same tree. Discovered by the `sase-su` epic land agent while running the
combined-tree verification for epic sase-su ("Drain stranded agents when an LLM
provider is disabled"); sase-su changes no provider-disable code
(`src/sase/llm_provider/provider_disable.py` and this test were last touched by
`4d945b1cd`, long before the epic), so the epic did not cause this.

ROOT CAUSE (precise, hence the `small` size): the test spawns six real Python
subprocesses and gates them on two hardcoded, unforgiving wall-clock timeouts
that cannot hold under the parallel lane's own contention:

- each worker polls for the `start` rendezvous file for at most `400 * 0.005s`
  = **2 seconds** before `raise SystemExit('start file never appeared')`
  (tests/test_provider_disable.py:146-151), and
- the parent then calls `process.communicate(timeout=10)` and asserts
  `process.returncode == 0` (tests/test_provider_disable.py:181-182).

Six fresh interpreter startups plus a `sase.llm_provider.provider_disable`
import each, racing four xdist workers and other agents' concurrent
`just check` runs on the same host, routinely exceed a 2s cold-start budget.
Nothing about first-writer correctness is being measured by those constants —
they are only a rendezvous. The fix is to derive both budgets from load (or
raise them substantially) and to replace the file-poll rendezvous with one that
cannot expire, so the test still proves "exactly one winner" without asserting
a machine-speed floor.

This is the same "fails under the full parallel lane, passes serially" class as
sase-pg, sase-qp, sase-qm, sase-qo, sase-qr, sase-sf, sase-si, sase-t3 and
sase-t6, but on a distinct node with its own concrete cause.

task_type_fields.evidence:
Fail rate 1/1 under the full parallel lane, 0/5 serially on the same tree.

- PARALLEL (failed): `just test` at HEAD ad9ed74af, clean tree, `pytest -n 4 --dist=worksteal -m 'not slow and not visual'`, on a host simultaneously running two other agents' `just check` invocations. Result: `2 failed, 36822 passed, 13 skipped in 1464.55s`; this node was one of the two (the other, tests/test_config_schema.py::test_default_config_matches_public_schema, is an unrelated confirmed schema drift already recorded on active epic sase-sp).
- SERIAL (passed 5/5): `for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly 'tests/test_provider_disable.py::test_facade_try_disable_one_winner_under_process_contention'; done` on the identical tree -> pass=5 fail=0. A single isolated rerun also passed in 4.56s (0.53s call).

Does not reproduce serially. Reproduces only under concurrent load, consistent with the 2s start-file poll and 10s communicate timeout described above.
